title: Support & License Mix Opportunity Mapper (scratch)
body:
Purpose
-----
Quick scratchpad to map where we might be leaving margin on the table by treating support and licensing as flat line items. Goal is a compact decision heuristic + example sims that we can hand to GTM and Solutions when sizing on-prem vs VPC deals. NOT final — lots of open assumptions.

Context + motivation
--------------------
- Many existing pricing exercises look at HW CAPEX and vm/costs but treat support as a percent of list price or a single band (e.g., 20%/30%). That glosses over large incremental ops costs for on‑prem installs (patching, appliance swap, local infra management) vs VPC (network egress, private peering, dedicated infra ops).
- Sales asks for 1–5 minute quick answers: "If I drop support to X or add managed-upgrade bundle, how does that change ARR breakeven / 3yr TCO?"
- Need heuristics + small spreadsheet that can be run without engineering (sheet + short checklist).

High-level decision levers to model (short list)
------------------------------------------------
1) Licensing model: perpetual license amortized vs term subscription
2) Support tiers: basic (email, SLA 72h), standard (SLA 24h + phone), premium (7x24 + on-call + RTO guarantees)
3) Managed services add-ons: managed upgrades, OS patching, DR runbook, emergency on-site
4) Hardware ops model: customer-owned HW vs Redwood-managed racks (lease + ops)
5) Network & data: cross-connect fees, egress, private link / peering, on-site firewall costs
6) Capacity buffer profile: hot spare vs thin-provision -> affects peak GPU count and capex
7) Amortization period and discount rate (3yr vs 5yr, WACC/IRR proxy)

Representative input assumptions (defaults for quick sim)
--------------------------------------------------------
- Target cluster: steady-state 8 A5200 GPUs serving 100 req/s (median)
- On-prem hardware list (incl racked infra): $420k initial (8x A5200 + network + storage + power)
- Redwood-managed hardware lease: $15k/month (includes ops + basic support)
- Licensing list (term model): $90k/yr base for equivalent capacity
- Licensing perpetual: $350k one-time, amortized over 5 years (straight-line)
- Support bands (annual): basic $18k, standard $36k, premium $90k
- Managed upgrades add-on: $12k/yr
- Customer infra ops estimate: 0.6 FTE equivalent for infra ops (salary + burden ~$140k/year) -> counted only for on-prem
- Network peering / egress: VPC model add $2k/mo typical for region + peering costs variable
- Discount rate for NPV: 8%

Quick scenario: 3-year Totals (rounded)
-------------------------------------
Scenario A: On‑prem, perpetual license, standard support, customer ops
- CAPEX hardware: $420k (year 0)
- License (perpetual amortized 5y): treat as $70k/yr -> $210k over 3y
- Support standard: $36k/yr -> $108k
- Customer infra ops FTE: $140k/yr -> $420k
- Managed upgrades: none
- Total 3yr (cash): 420 + 210 + 108 + 420 = $1,158k
- Equivalent annualized ~$386k/yr

Scenario B: VPC (Redwood-managed), subscription license, premium support incl. managed upgrades
- Redwood lease (capex-free): $15k/mo -> $540k over 3y
- License subscription: $90k/yr -> $270k
- Support premium: $90k/yr -> $270k
- Managed upgrades included (no extra)
- Customer infra ops: 0 FTE
- Total 3yr (cash): 540 + 270 + 270 = $1,080k
- Equivalent annualized ~$360k/yr

Initial finding (toy example):
- Despite a high headline for managed lease, VPC path is slightly cheaper over 3 years in this config because we avoided the FTE ops line and the heavy up-front capex. The break even shifts with different amortization or if customer values CAPEX for tax reasons.

Sensitivity notes (what flips the decision)
-----------------------------------------
- If the customer can re-use existing GPU cluster (CAPEX sunk), on‑prem becomes >50% cheaper immediately.
- If support is reduced to "basic" for on-prem (assume 10k/yr) and customer provides 0.3 FTE ops instead of 0.6, the on‑prem 3yr falls below VPC.
- If hardware cost drops 20% (couponing, OEM deal) on‑prem becomes clearly cheaper.

Heuristics for Sales / Solutions (one‑page script)
--------------------------------------------------
- Quick intake questions (2 min): existing GPU investment? tolerance for upfront spend? compliance/regulatory reasons for VPC vs on‑prem? ops headcount availability? desired SLA? preferred contract term length?
- Rapid mapping rule-of-thumb: If customer already has >4 usable GPUs or values CAPEX depreciation -> favor on‑prem. If customer has <4 GPUs and no ops team -> favor Redwood-managed VPC.
- Bundling guidance: convert premium support + managed upgrades into a single "Ops+" add-on priced at ~12% of subscription to make comparisons easier and reduce friction.

Optimization recommendations (concrete changes to current bundle matrix)
------------------------------------------------------------------------
1) Introduce a "hybrid-managed" bundle for on‑prem: keeps license on-prem but adds a remote-managed ops layer (monthly fee) priced at ~40% of Redwood-managed lease price (cheaper than full lease, still avoids FTE).
2) Re-tier support pricing into narrower bands with discrete features (SLA windows, runbook updates, security patching) so that we can unbundle and price optional add-ons (reduces buyer friction).
3) Add a short amortization slider in the quicksheet (1/3/5 yr) and a checkbox for "customer has working GPU farm" that zeros hardware CAPEX.
4) Put a small performance credit for customers taking managed upgrades continuously (faster engine optimizations rolled in) — communicates quantifiable value vs self-ops.

Open questions / data pulls required
------------------------------------
- Confirm typical on-prem infra ops comp and burden across region: is 0.6 FTE the right baseline? (ask SRE hiring comp) -> @SRE-peopleops
- Get anonymized deal data: 30 most recent private-deploy deals (license, support tier, managed addon, on-prem vs vpc) to fit real distributions -> JIRA/CRM pull (request to RevOps)
- Vendor HW discount bands: procurement team to share typical OEM rebate levels for GPU purchases at 8–32 GPU intervals
- Legal: are there constraints on offering a "hybrid-managed" bundle (service commitments, indemnities)?

Next steps (owner/timeline)
---------------------------
- Maya: build quick Google Sheet prototype with knobs (amortization, FTE ops slider, support tiers) by 2024-10-18
- Liam: pull CRM deal export for last 24 months (private deploys) by 2024-10-12
- Sofia: draft language for hybrid-managed bundle and suggested pricing floor by 2024-10-20
- Ravi: check legal/regulatory flags for on-site support commitments by 2024-10-21

Notes to self (scratch)
----------------------
- Might be useful to surface a small NPV delta threshold (e.g., >10% 3yr cost advantage) to justify taking a product discount vs baseline.
- Customer psychology: some customers prefer CAPEX for predictable costs and tax treatment; treat that as a negotiation axis, not purely numeric.
- Need a clean 1-slide summary for AE playbook: 6-question intake + green/red rules for quick decision.

References and in-app hooks
---------------------------
- Quicksheet should link to (1) internal SKU table, (2) a short checklist for security/physical access needed for on-prem (see confluence link above), and (3) sample SOW language for hybrid-managed that sales can use as starting point.

Unresolved: pricing elasticity to support tier pricing — we don't have enough A/B test data; consider running a small pilot with two customers for 6 months.

-- end of scratchpad --
